summary: Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Harvard University by 2003, studying under Leonard van der Kuijp, Charles Hallisey, and Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and held a fellowship at Grinnell College.

Ivo Fišer (1929–2011) was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as a lecturer at Charles University around 1960 and was affiliated with the University of Copenhagen's Institute for Indian Philology around 1970.

Iwao Ishikawa specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. His career includes positions as a researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2000, 2026) and lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Iwao Nakajima (born 1934) studied under Nichiki Kimura and earned a master's degree from Hitotsubashi University. Active in Buddhist studies, he worked at the NHK Broadcasting Culture Research Institute until 1975 and served as director at Sandhaan (attested 1999).

Iwao Shima (1950–2007) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Nagoya University. He spent his career at Kanazawa University, holding positions from around 1982 to 1993 and serving as professor from around 1993 to 2007.

Izumi Hoshi (born 1967) specializes in Tibetology and linguistics. She completed her undergraduate and graduate studies at the University of Tokyo between roughly 1987 and 1997, and served as assistant professor (1997) and director (2019–2023) at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.

Izumi Matsuda-Kiami is a scholar in Japanology and linguistics who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. She has served as a teaching professor at the University of Washington, with affiliation attested in 2026.

J. A. B. van Buitenen (1928–1979) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He earned his doctorate under Jan Gonda at Utrecht University (1946–1953), later serving as reader there (1959–1961) and as a distinguished service professor at the University of Chicago.

J. B. Disanayaka (born 1937) is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Colombo from around 1970 to 2002, and his affiliation with SOAS University of London is attested in 1996.

J. G. Jennings worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as principal of Muir Central College and as Director of Public Instruction for the Department of Public Instruction, Bihar and Orissa, attested in 1918.

J. Gordon Melton (born 1942), a religious studies scholar, studied at Birmingham-Southern College, Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary, and Northwestern University. He founded the Institute for the Study of American Religion and held posts at UC Santa Barbara and Baylor University.

J. L. Shaw specializes in philosophy and Indology. Shaw studied at Rice University, was taught by Bimal Krishna Matilal around 1968 to 1973, and held a position at Victoria University of Wellington around 1976.
J. M. E. McTaggart (1866–1925) was a philosopher who studied at Clifton College between 1882 and 1885. He held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from roughly 1891 until 1923.

J. N. Farquhar (1861–1929) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. His education included studies at Aberdeen Grammar School, the University of Aberdeen from around 1883 to 1885, and Christ Church from around 1885 to 1889.

J. P. Mallory (born 1945) works in archaeology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Occidental College and UCLA before serving as Professor of Prehistoric Archaeology at Queen's University Belfast from circa 1977 to 2011.

J. Robert Oppenheimer (1904–1967) studied at Harvard, Cambridge, and Göttingen, and studied Sanskrit under Arthur W. Ryder. He held posts at UC Berkeley, Caltech, the Manhattan Project (1942–1945), and the Institute for Advanced Study (1947–1966).

J. S. Negi is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Ram Shankar Tripathi. Negi conducted research at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University around 1977 and served as chief editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1993–2001).
J. S. Pade was an Indologist. He held positions as a research officer at the University of Chicago (attested in 1963) and at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested in 1966).

J. Thomas Rimer (born 1933) is a Japanologist who studied at Princeton and Columbia. He held posts at Washington University in St. Louis (~1971–1983), the University of Maryland (~1988–1999), and the University of Pittsburgh (~1999–2011).

Jack Goody (1919–2015) was a scholar in archaeology and religious studies. He was educated at St Albans School and St John's College, Cambridge, and served as a professor at the University of Cambridge from roughly 1973 to 1984.
